create.title: Nonzero residue-offset energy reduced to a centred nonzero dual difference
create.statement_tex: Let J=sqrt(X), Q=J^(2/5), T=J^(3/5), B=C/T, and J^(13/18)<C<=J^(3/4). For every compatible smooth-interior nonaxial M1 component and local class kappa in {1/4,1/2,1}, put g_kappa=4kappa, M_kappa=4b/g_kappa, and c=g_kappa x. After the accepted reciprocal correction is absorbed into e(plus-or-minus A_(kappa,b)/c), the exact local unit is zeta e_(M_kappa)(K_kappa bar(x)), with (g,M,K)=(1,4b,k), (2,2b,2[k bar(4)]_b), or (4,b,[k bar(4)]_b). Exact progression Poisson gives M^(-1) sum_n S(n,K;M)I_b(n). Removing the residue offset a=0 once is exactly the same-residue mode. The remaining energy splits into a literal integer difference d=0 and Y_C=M^(-2) sum_(b asymp B) sum_(d not equal 0) sum_n (S(n+d,K;M)conj(S(n,K;M))-c_M(d)) I_b(n+d)conj(I_b(n)). Sampled Parseval plus the reciprocal autocorrelation phase gives sum_n|I_b(n)|^2 <<_epsilon X^epsilon M C/g. Therefore the d=0 slice is <<_epsilon X^epsilon B^2 C=X^epsilon C^3/T^2, target-safe throughout the frozen band; the standard Weil-Estermann bound sharpens it to X^epsilon BC. Nonzero multiples d congruent 0 mod M remain in Y_C. The first exact smooth-main survivor is Y_C with target <<_epsilon X^epsilon J^2/T. Complete offset Fourier transformation and inversion are self-returns in all three classes. No B-power gain, conductor extension, transition or axial estimate, cone-edge estimate, full M9-M1, M9, or exponent is proved.
create.next_action: Estimate the centred d!=0 Kloosterman-product correlation with the actual stationary Fourier weights. Any B^(-delta) gain must preserve the inherited Q^(-5/12) row saving and treat nonzero d congruent 0 mod M and gcd-degenerate modes explicitly.

update.statement_tex: Let J=sqrt(X), Q=J^(2/5), T=J^(3/5), and J^(13/18)<C<=J. In the first band J^(13/18)<C<=J^(3/4), the exact transition error and axes are separately target-safe. For each fixed smooth nonaxial local component, rescale the three arithmetic classes to inverse units modulo M in {4b,2b,b} and Poisson-sum the actual reciprocal row. The complete same-residue mode and the literal dual difference d=0 are target-safe. Thus the first-band principal energy is exactly reduced to Y_C=M^(-2) sum_b sum_(d not equal 0) sum_n (S(n+d,K;M)conj(S(n,K;M))-c_M(d)) I_b(n+d)conj(I_b(n)), with target Y_C<<_epsilon X^epsilon J^2/T. Nonzero multiples d congruent 0 mod M, gcd-degenerate modes, and every coherent nonzero offset remain in Y_C. The inherited absolute offset capacity is X^epsilon C^3/(TQ^(5/12)); a signed B^(-delta) gain is still required. On J^(3/4)<C<=J, the principal main, transition error, and axes all require signed control. This proves no estimate for Y_C, no conductor extension, no cone edge, full M9-M1, M9, or exponent.
update.next_action: Attack the centred nonzero-dual-difference actual-weight correlation in J^(13/18)<C<=J^(3/4), then return to the upper band where transitions and axes also remain open.
Close the centred d!=0 Kloosterman-product correlation in the first upper-conductor band, then treat C>J^(3/4), cone edges, remaining radial sectors, and endpoint uniformity.

The coherent nonzero-offset energy has now been further reduced by removing the literal dual difference d=0. Estimate the centred d!=0 correlation in M9-M1-nonzero-residue-offset-dual-difference-reduction.

reject.reason: For q=4p^nu and a=4p^(nu-1)alpha with p not dividing k alpha, the zero additive-frequency rational sum has size q^(1-1/(2nu)+o(1)); in particular q^(3/4+o(1)) at nu=2 and q^(7/8+o(1)) at nu=4. Any usable bound must retain gcd degeneracies and average with the actual weights.

The all-offset kernel is the rank-one form |sum_r u(r)R(r)|^2-sum_r|R(r)|^2, and arbitrary phase-conjugating weights saturate it. A proof must use the actual reciprocal Fourier weights, not only coefficient norms or complete-sum moments.
A B^(-1/2) gain reaches only C<=J^(56/75). The upper endpoint C=J^(3/4) requires at least B^(-5/9).

The exact product-Kloosterman Fourier transform followed by inversion returns the original nonzero residue-offset row in all three local classes. Only an estimate after the transform can save a power.
The proved target-safe slice is the literal integer difference d=0. Terms d!=0 with d congruent 0 mod M remain in the centred correlation and cannot be discarded as the same zero mode.
The c congruent 2 mod 4 and 4|c units require separate rescalings to moduli 2b and b. Their exact coefficients follow from bs_0+rho=tc and cannot be inferred by copying the odd modulus 4b formula.

no_change.reason: The first residual band is narrowed to a centred d!=0 actual-weight correlation, but no estimate or conductor extension is proved; upper conductors, cone edges, other radial sectors, and endpoint uniformity remain open.
Round 83 concerns only the M1 transition-flattened upper-conductor principal energy.
Both M9-M1 and M9-M2 remain open.
The round proves a structural M1 reduction but no new global Gauss-circle exponent.

round_assessment.reason: The round proves no B-power saving and no new conductor range, but it derives the two even inverse units exactly, removes a complete target-safe dual slice, and replaces the raw nonzero-offset energy by a strictly smaller all-class centred d!=0 Kloosterman-product correlation. Prime-power degeneracies, rank-one self-return, and current-source failures are recorded without overclaiming M9-M1 or the exponent.
